alarmsT3d.source_note: Source: T3D V2.0 commissioning manual, chapter 5. The servo panel shows the same code (Err-- = no alarm). Encoder and power alarms cannot be cleared over the bus: remove the cause and power cycle the servo. Tap a row to see what to do.

diagnosis.pyserial_is_missing_in_the_plugin: pyserial is missing in the plugin environment.
diagnosis.pick_the_adapter_in_buses_and: Pick the adapter in Buses and adapters and save.
diagnosis.this_bus_has_no_adapter_chosen: This bus has no adapter chosen.
diagnosis.unplug_the_adapter_and_plug_it: Unplug the adapter and plug it back in. If it continues, read the message below.
diagnosis.close_the_other_program_or_remove: Close the other program (or remove the other bus that uses the same adapter): the system must be the only one using it.
diagnosis.the_adapter_is_there_but_another: The adapter is there, but another program is using it.
diagnosis.the_adapter_is_there_but_the: The adapter is there, but the service is not allowed to use it.
diagnosis.plug_it_into_a_usb_port: Plug it into a USB port of the system (or try another cable or USB port). While it is missing, the system retries less and less often, without loading the processor.
diagnosis.adapter_not_found_the_system_does: Adapter not found: the system does not see this bus's USB-RS485 adapter.
diagnosis.search_all_addresses_below_or_add: Search all addresses (below) or add the device in Devices.
diagnosis.adapter_connected_there_are_no_devices: Adapter connected; there are no devices configured on this bus yet.
diagnosis.they_are_not_watched_and_do: They are not watched and do not count as faults. When you connect them, tap Watch again.
diagnosis.adapter_connected_every_device_on_this: Adapter connected; every device on this bus is marked as absent.
diagnosis.if_nothing_is_connected_to_the: If nothing is connected to the cable on purpose, mark the devices as absent and it stops counting as a fault. If something should be there: check that it is on, the A/B wiring (try swapping them), the common ground and the speed and format (use Search all addresses).
diagnosis.adapter_connected_but_no_device_answers: Adapter connected, but no device answers.
diagnosis.check_that_it_is_on_its: Check that it is on, its address and the cable to it. If it is not connected on purpose, mark it as absent.
diagnosis.the_adapter_works_but_some_device: The adapter works, but some device does not answer.
diagnosis.all_good_the_adapter_works_and: All good: the adapter works and every device answers.
diagnosis.create_a_bus_with_this_adapter: Create a bus with this adapter, speed and format
diagnosis.it_answers_with_a_different_format: It answers with a different format than the bus: change the bus speed and format to use it
diagnosis.no_address_answered_check_that_the: No address answered. Check that the device is on, the A/B wiring (try swapping them) and the common ground (GND).
diagnosis.on_the_duet_s_rs485_the: On the Duet's RS485 the speed is set by M575: it only searches with the bus speed.
diagnosis.asks_address_by_address_whether_anyone: Asks address by address whether anyone answers, with the speed and format you pick (or all of them). It is slow and only runs when you ask; devices that already work keep being read in between.
diagnosis.no_buses_yet_create_one_in: No buses yet: create one in Buses and adapters.
diagnosis.it_answers_now_you_can_watch: It answers now: you can watch it again.
diagnosis.it_may_be_another_program_or: It may be another program or master on the same cable, electrical noise, or loose A/B wires. The system must be the only master.
diagnosis.cable_is_quiet_nobody_else_is: Cable is quiet (nobody else is talking)
diagnosis.the_duet_did_not_accept_the: The Duet did not accept the port setup (M575)
diagnosis.the_duet_accepted_the_port_setup: The Duet accepted the port setup (M575)
diagnosis.if_it_is_the_same_one: If it is the same one with another name, pick it in the bus (Buses and adapters tab).
diagnosis.checking_the_adapter_and_asking_each: Checking the adapter and asking each device...
diagnosis.checks_each_bus_step_by_step: Checks each bus step by step: whether the adapter is connected, whether the port opens, whether data arrives and which devices answer. Read only: it changes nothing on the devices.
diagnosis.help_page_what: A step-by-step check of each bus: is the adapter connected, does the port open, is anything talking on the cable, and which configured devices answer. It only reads; it changes nothing on the devices.
diagnosis.help_page_why: To find out where the chain breaks (adapter, permission, cable, address, speed) instead of guessing.
diagnosis.help_page_how: Press Diagnose on a bus and read the verdict at the top, then the steps. Use the search below if you do not know a device address.
diagnosis.help_sweep_what: Asks address by address (from - to) whether anyone answers, with the speed and format you pick, or with all of them. It is slow and only runs when you ask; the devices that already work keep being read in between.
diagnosis.help_sweep_why: To discover a device whose address, speed or format you do not know.
diagnosis.help_sweep_how: Choose the bus, the range of addresses and the wait per address (ms), then Find. The answering ones appear as chips; tap one to add it as a device.

device.could_not_load_the_servo_table: Could not load the servo table:
device.data_parameters_and_alarms_of_this: Data, parameters and alarms of this device (plus the registers added by hand) in a file to share or use on another machine.
device.the_t3d_parameters_and_alarms_in: The T3D parameters and alarms in the common format: a good example for another device.
device.reads_a_range_of_registers_and: Reads a range of registers and shows the ones that exist with their current value (without changing anything). One tap adds one to the watched ones. The other devices keep being watched meanwhile.
device.asks_the_device_for_its_maker: Asks the device for its maker and model (Modbus function 43). Many drives and meters answer it.
device.it_did_not_answer_the_identification: It did not answer the identification: the device does not support it (or it is on a Duet bus, which only reads registers).
device.read_or_write_a_register_by: Read or write a register by hand
device.the_torque_and_current_charts_appear: The torque and current charts appear as soon as servo readings arrive (since you opened the page).
device.the_charts_appear_after_a_few_readings: The charts appear after a few readings (since you opened the page).
device.mark_a_parameter_or_state_to_chart: Nothing is charted yet: mark a state with "chart": true, or a parameter with "watch": true, in the device profile.
device.tap_again_to_clear_the_alarm: Tap again to clear the alarm
device.moves_no_axis_the_machine_can: · moves no axis: the machine can keep working
device.absent_on_purpose_it_is_not: Absent on purpose: it is not watched and does not count as a fault. It is tried once a minute.
device.the_system_found_it_and_added: The system found it and added it by itself: check name and axis
device.axis_faults_pause: Its faults pause jobs and block homing of this axis
device.no_axis_faults_warn: It moves no axis: its faults only warn
device.alarm_not_in_manual: alarm not documented in the manual
device.no_registers_defined: No registers defined: it is still checked that it answers (reads register {n}). Use Explore registers (below) to see which ones it has, or Edit to add them by hand.
device.alarm_still_active: The alarm is still active (Err{n}): remove the cause or power cycle the servo.
device.written_but_reads: It was written, but reading it back gives {v}
device.help_alarm_what: The alarm code the device reports right now. "None" means no active alarm; a number is looked up in the alarm table (for the T3D servo it is the same Err-- code shown on its panel).
device.help_alarm_why: An active alarm is a fault: it can pause the job according to the monitoring options.
device.help_alarm_how: When there is one, the box below tells what happens, what to do and how it clears. See all codes in the Alarm codes tab.
device.help_torque_what: The torque the servo is delivering, in percent, with the highest peak seen and the limit set in Edit.
device.help_torque_why: Torque above the limit usually means a jam or a collision, and counts as a fault.
device.help_torque_how: The bar turns orange near the limit. Change the limit in Edit > Monitoring.
device.help_current_what: The motor current the servo is drawing, in amperes, with a small chart of the recent values.
device.help_current_why: If a limit is set, going above it counts as a fault; without a limit it is only shown.
device.help_current_how: Set or clear the limit in Edit > Monitoring.
device.help_if_fails_what: The action chosen for a fault of this device (pause the job and warn, just warn or nothing) and, below it, how often it is read and how many readings have been made.
device.help_if_fails_why: It is the monitoring set in Edit, shown here so you know what will happen.

deviceEditor.profile_removed_the_watched_registers_st: Profile removed (the watched registers stay). Tap Save to keep it.
deviceEditor.the_example_was_downloaded_open_it: The example was downloaded: open it to see the format, change it for your device and import it.
deviceEditor.just_warn_you_pause_in_the: Just warn (you pause in the sending program)
deviceEditor.a_json_file_with_the_device: A JSON file with the device data, the parameter table and the alarm table. It fills everything at once; what it doesn't bring you complete by hand. To see the format, export the profile of a T3D servo or tap Example.
deviceEditor.a_job_run_from_a_file: A job run from a file is paused (M25). A live job arrives line by line and the machine can't pause it: there you choose between just warning (you pause in the sending program) or emergency stop (M112, cuts everything).
deviceEditor.losing_communication_is_also_a_fault: Losing communication is also a fault
deviceEditor.if_the_job_is_live_no: If the job is live (no file)
deviceEditor.after_changing_them_on_the_panel: After changing them on the panel, power-cycle the servo.
deviceEditor.the_t3d_servo_only_supports_4800: The T3D servo only supports 4800-115200 baud and 8N1 / 8E1 / 8O1 with 1 stop bit: change the bus.
deviceEditor.on_the_servo_panel_set_exactly: On the servo panel set exactly this (otherwise it will not answer):
deviceEditor.there_are_no_buses_yet_create: There are no buses yet. Create one in the tab
deviceEditor.they_do_not_pause_jobs_do: (they do not pause jobs, do not block homing and count as a warning, not a fault).
deviceEditor.if_this_device_fails_the_job: If this device fails: the job is paused according to the monitoring below, it counts as
deviceEditor.fault_explain: on the status lights, and a homing of axis {axis} (G28) is cancelled with a message instead of waiting for the endstop.
deviceEditor.fault_explain_no_lights: and a homing of axis {axis} (G28) is cancelled with a message instead of waiting for the endstop.
deviceEditor.if_fails_while_axis_moves: If it fails while axis {axis} is moving (home, jog)
deviceEditor.absent_hint: Not connected on purpose: it is not watched and does not count as a fault (it is tried once a minute)
deviceEditor.bus_mismatch: The profile says the device comes at {wants} and this bus is at {has}: change one of them so they understand each other.
deviceEditor.profile_applied: {origin}. Check it and tap Save to keep it.
deviceEditor.n_registers_kept: The {n} registers you already had are kept.
deviceEditor.other_device_json_hint: Another device (not a T3D servo)? Choose «Generic Modbus»: «Import JSON» appears there to load its profile file, with an example to download.
deviceEditor.profile_row_kept: Registers you added by hand that stay
deviceEditor.profile_row_after_value: It is loaded in this editor; tap Save to keep it.
deviceEditor.profile_replaces_loaded: It replaces the profile loaded now ({name}).
deviceEditor.profile_empty: The profile has no parameters and no alarm codes.
deviceEditor.help_profile_what: The kind of device on the bus. "T3D servo" already knows its parameters, alarms and live states; "Generic Modbus" is any other device whose registers you list or load from a JSON profile.
deviceEditor.help_profile_why: It decides which tabs the device gets (states, parameters, alarms) and how it is read.
deviceEditor.help_profile_how: It is chosen when the device is created and cannot be changed afterwards: to change it, remove the device and add it again.
deviceEditor.help_axis_what: The machine axis that this device drives (for example the servo of the Z axis). "None" if it is not tied to an axis.
deviceEditor.help_axis_why: With an axis, a failure of this device pauses the job according to the monitoring below and cancels a homing (G28) of that axis with a message instead of waiting for the endstop. Without an axis, a failure is only a warning: it does not pause jobs nor block homing.
deviceEditor.help_axis_how: Pick the axis letter that this device really moves.
deviceEditor.help_bus_what: The RS485 bus, that is the adapter (or the Duet RS485 port), where this device is wired.
deviceEditor.help_bus_why: Each bus has one speed and format, so all its devices must be set the same.
deviceEditor.help_bus_how: Create or edit the buses in the "Buses and adapters" tab.
deviceEditor.help_address_what: The Modbus address of the device on its bus, from 1 to 247.
deviceEditor.help_address_why: The system asks each address in turn; two devices with the same address on one bus answer on top of each other.
deviceEditor.help_address_how: Use the number set on the device itself (for the T3D servo, parameter P-181). "Scan bus" below lists the addresses that answer; tap one to fill it in.
deviceEditor.help_scan_what: Asks addresses 1 to 32 of the chosen bus whether anyone answers, and lists the ones that do.
deviceEditor.help_scan_why: To find the address of a device you do not know, or to check the wiring.
deviceEditor.help_scan_how: Choose the bus first. The answering numbers appear as chips; tap one to use it as this device address.
deviceEditor.help_on_fault_what: What the system does when this device reports a fault (an alarm, a value over its limit, or lost communication): pause the job and warn, just warn, or nothing (only show it).
deviceEditor.help_on_fault_why: Lets a servo failure stop the job before it damages the part or the machine.
deviceEditor.help_on_fault_how: This applies to a job run from a file, which is paused (M25). A live job is set by the next option.
deviceEditor.help_in_live_title: If the job is live (not pausable)
deviceEditor.help_in_live_what: What to do on a fault when the job arrives line by line from a program (a live job): the machine cannot pause it.
deviceEditor.help_in_live_why: A file job can be paused; a live one cannot, so you choose between warning only or cutting everything.
deviceEditor.help_in_live_how: "Just warn" means you pause it in the sending program. "Emergency stop (M112)" cuts everything at once.
deviceEditor.help_in_motion_title: If it fails while the axis moves
deviceEditor.help_in_motion_what: What to do when this device fails while its axis is moving without a job (homing, jog).
deviceEditor.help_in_motion_why: A servo that fails during a move can leave the axis running or hit the end of travel.
deviceEditor.help_in_motion_how: "Just warn" only notifies; "Emergency stop (M112)" cuts everything at once.
deviceEditor.help_comm_fault_title: Losing communication is also a fault
deviceEditor.help_comm_fault_what: If on, a device that stops answering counts as a fault, with the same action as any other fault.
deviceEditor.help_comm_fault_why: A silent servo may be powered off or unplugged while the job keeps running without protection.
deviceEditor.help_comm_fault_how: Turn it off for a device that is often switched off on purpose (or mark it absent).
deviceEditor.help_poll_what: The pause between two readings of this device, in seconds (minimum 0.1).
deviceEditor.help_poll_why: Shorter means faster detection of a fault but more traffic on the bus.
deviceEditor.help_poll_how: The default of the profile (0.5 s for the T3D servo) is fine for most machines.
deviceEditor.help_comm_limit_what: How many readings in a row must go unanswered before the device is declared without communication.
deviceEditor.help_comm_limit_why: A single lost message due to noise should not stop a job; a number of them in a row should.
deviceEditor.help_comm_limit_how: Raise it on noisy cables; lower it for a faster reaction.
deviceEditor.help_torque_what: Torque limit of the servo, in percent. If the measured torque goes above it, that is a fault.
deviceEditor.help_torque_why: A torque above the limit usually means a jam or a collision.
deviceEditor.help_torque_how: The default is 150 %. Set it lower to react earlier to a jam.
deviceEditor.help_current_what: Current limit of the servo, in amperes. If the measured current goes above it, that is a fault. Empty means the current is not watched.
deviceEditor.help_current_why: A current peak above the expected one warns of overload before the drive trips by itself.
deviceEditor.help_current_how: Leave it empty if you do not know the motor current.
deviceEditor.help_json_profile_what: A JSON file that describes a Generic Modbus device: its data, a table of parameters and a table of alarm codes. Optional.
deviceEditor.help_json_profile_why: It fills the parameters and alarms tabs and the watched registers in one go, instead of typing every register by hand.
deviceEditor.help_json_profile_how: Import JSON loads your file; Example downloads one to see the format; Remove profile drops it (the watched registers stay). Tap Save to keep the change.
deviceEditor.help_records_what: The Modbus registers of the device that are read continuously: name, register number, function (3 holding or 4 input), scale, unit and optional limits. "Write" lets the panel change that register.
deviceEditor.help_records_why: They are the values shown for the device and the ones checked for faults when min or max are set.
deviceEditor.help_records_how: Take the register numbers from the device manual. The scale multiplies the raw number to get the unit (0.1 turns 215 into 21.5).
deviceEditor.help_absent_what: Marks a device that is not connected right now, on purpose.
deviceEditor.help_absent_why: It is not watched, so it does not count as a fault and does not pause jobs. The system still tries it once a minute to notice when it comes back.
deviceEditor.help_absent_how: Use it for a spare or removable device; switch it off when it is connected again.

statesT3d.values_that_just_changed_are_highlighted: Values that just changed are highlighted for a moment. These are the servo's monitoring variables (d- menu on the panel), read over RS485 once per second while this tab is open. Hover over a row to see the Modbus register.

startupGuide.it_is_read_every_few_seconds: It is read every few seconds without failures. Faults go to the status lights, Activity and the phone.
startupGuide.it_is_read_every_few_seconds_no_lights: It is read every few seconds without failures. Faults go to Activity and the phone.
startupGuide.it_is_read_every_few_seconds_no_activity: It is read every few seconds without failures. Faults go to the status lights and the phone.
startupGuide.it_is_read_every_few_seconds_no_lights_n: It is read every few seconds without failures. Faults go to the phone.
startupGuide.returns_everything_as_json_faults_go_no_: has everything (a macro reads it with that expression). Faults go to the event log (and reach your phone).
startupGuide.one_does_not_answer_check_address: One does not answer: check address, speed and format (on the servo: P-181/182/183) and the A/B wiring. Use "Search" in Buses.
startupGuide.add_your_device_for_example_the: Add your device (for example the T3D servo) in Devices.
startupGuide.a_bus_does_not_open_check: A bus does not open: check that the chosen port is the adapter's.
startupGuide.there_is_no_bus_yet_create: There is no bus yet. Create it in Buses and adapters.
startupGuide.the_service_is_missing_the_dialout: The service is missing the dialout group. Once, on the system (SSH):
startupGuide.the_service_is_in_the_dialout: The service is in the dialout group.
startupGuide.could_not_check_if_the_bus: Could not check (if the bus opens, it is fine).
startupGuide.not_needed_with_the_duet_s: Not needed with the Duet's RS485.
startupGuide.permission_to_use_the_serial_port: Permission to use the serial port
startupGuide.the_system_does_not_see_any: The system does not see any USB-RS485 adapter. Plug it into a USB port on the system and tap Refresh.
startupGuide.you_use_the_duet_s_rs485: You use the Duet's RS485: no USB adapter needed.
startupGuide.not_responding_check_in_plugins_that: Not responding. Check in Plugins that WorkshopRS485 is started.
startupGuide.returns_everything_as_json_faults_go: has everything (a macro reads it with that expression). Faults go to the event log (and reach Activity and your phone).
startupGuide.t3d_servo_brings_its_own_logic: "T3D servo" brings its own logic (alarm, torque, current, P-xxx parameters). "Generic Modbus" works for anything else: you pick which registers to read, their scale, unit and limits.
startupGuide.which_does_not_change_if_you: , which does not change if you plug it into another USB.
startupGuide.plug_it_in_and_it_shows: plug it in and it shows up above in Buses and adapters (with "Detect" or "Create bus by hand"). It is chosen by its name in
startupGuide.and_warns_you_then_you_set: and warns you: then you set its name and axis in Edit. If you do not want to wait, tap "Search everything now".
startupGuide.the_6hc_v1_02c_and_the: the 6HC v1.02c (and the 6XD v1.02) have a built-in RS485. In Buses choose "Duet RS485 port": the board acts as master and no adapter is needed on the system. It is a bit slower than the USB adapter (every reading goes through the board), so for very frequent monitoring USB is better.
startupGuide.all_at_the_same_baud_rate: all at the same baud rate and format, each with a different address (1-247). Add them as devices of the same bus.
startupGuide.and_a_common_ground_gnd_if: and a common ground (GND). If nothing answers, try swapping A and B. On a long bus, a 120 Ω resistor between A and B at both ends.
startupGuide.a_to_a_d_b_to: A to A (D+), B to B (D-)
startupGuide.usb_rs485_adapter_e_g_ft232rl: USB-RS485 adapter (e.g. FT232RL / E810-U15) in a USB port on the system. From the adapter to the device:
startupGuide.more_details_wiring_several_devices_duet: More details (wiring, several devices, Duet, macros)
startupGuide.the_steps_tick_themselves_as_the: The steps tick themselves as the system checks them. If one stays orange, that is where the problem is.
startupGuide.another_device_text: with automatic detection on (Buses and adapters) there is nothing to do: if it goes on a bus you already have, the system finds it in a couple of minutes (at the speed of that bus, so the device must be configured the same and with a free address); if it is a new adapter, it tries every speed and creates its bus. It adds it
startupGuide.read_but_in_fault: It is read every few seconds, but {list} is in fault: check its card in Devices.

historyT3d.last_500_events_of_all_devices: , last 500 events of all devices). The servo keeps its last 10 alarms, but they are only shown on its panel (the manual does not document how to read them over RS485).

paramsT3d.is_not_a_t3d_parameter_backup: is not a T3D parameter backup
paramsT3d.the_backup_matches_what_the_servo: The backup matches what the servo has: nothing to change.
paramsT3d.saved_in_the_servo_eeprom_the: Saved in the servo EEPROM: the changes stay even when it is powered off.
paramsT3d.mentioned_in_the_manual_text_no: Mentioned in the manual text, no documented range.
paramsT3d.tap_again_store_in_the_servo: Tap again: store in the servo
paramsT3d.they_re_lost_when_the_servo: : they're lost when the servo is turned off.
paramsT3d.nothing_to_show_with_this_filter: Nothing to show with this filter.
paramsT3d.the_servo_answers_0x5a53_it_does: The servo answers 0x5A53: it does not have this value
paramsT3d.if_you_change_the_address_baud: If you change the address, baud rate or format, the servo stops answering with the current settings: save to EEPROM, restart the servo and also change the device / bus on this page.
paramsT3d.invalid_values_according_to_the_manual: Invalid values according to the manual
paramsT3d.there_are_no_backups_of_this: There are no backups of this servo yet.
paramsT3d.save_what_was_read_to_the: Save what was read to the SD
paramsT3d.search_number_name_or_word_e: Search: number, name or word (e.g. gain, 181)
paramsT3d.reading_from_servo: Reading from the servo... register {n} of {total}
paramsT3d.internal_registers_note: Registers the servo has but the manual ({manual}) does not document: factory settings. They are shown so you can back them up and compare them; they cannot be edited from here.
paramsT3d.has_effect_in_mode: It has effect in the current servo mode
paramsT3d.no_effect_in_mode: It has no effect in the current mode ({modes})
paramsT3d.current_value_invalid: Current value invalid according to the manual: {why}
paramsT3d.reading_stopped_check: The reading stopped: {error}. Check the servo connection.
paramsT3d.n_written_verified: {n} change(s) written and verified. Test them and then save them to EEPROM.
paramsT3d.backup_values_as_changes: Backup of {date}: {n} different value(s) were left as changes. Check them and tap "Write to the servo".
paramsT3d.backup_after_value: The values go to the list of changes; nothing is written to the servo until you tap Write to the servo.
paramsT3d.backup_nothing_changes: Nothing would change: the file matches what the servo has, or holds only registers that cannot be written.
paramsT3d.backup_other_device: The file is from device {device}; this one is {current}.
paramsT3d.backup_not_read: The servo has not been read yet: every value of the file counts as a change.
paramsT3d.backup_out_of_range: {n} value(s) are not allowed by the manual: they will show as invalid and need the force option to be written.
paramsT3d.backup_replaces_typed: {n} value(s) you typed and have not written will be replaced.
paramsT3d.backup_ignored: {n} entries of the file are not a register of the servo or not a whole number and are ignored.
paramsT3d.help_read_what: All the parameters of the T3D servo, read one by one over RS485 and grouped. Each shows its value, its range from the manual and the risk of changing it.
paramsT3d.help_read_why: To check or tune the servo from here instead of its small panel.
paramsT3d.help_read_how: Read all again refreshes the values. Changes are only collected until you press "Write to the servo"; "Save to EEPROM" then makes them permanent.
paramsT3d.help_write_what: Sends the changes you typed to the servo, one by one, and reads each one back to check it was accepted.
paramsT3d.help_write_why: Until then nothing changes on the servo; Discard drops them.
paramsT3d.help_write_missing: A written value lives only in the servo RAM: it is lost when the servo is switched off until you save it to EEPROM.
paramsT3d.help_write_how: Write, test the machine, then press Save to EEPROM. A value outside the manual range needs the "Force invalid values" box (admin only).
paramsT3d.help_eeprom_what: Stores in the servo permanent memory the values already written.
paramsT3d.help_eeprom_why: Without it, the written values are lost when the servo is powered off.
paramsT3d.help_eeprom_how: Tap twice (the second tap confirms). Test the changes before saving them.
paramsT3d.help_backups_what: A copy of the values read from the servo, saved on the Pi SD card (with an optional note) or as a JSON file you download.
paramsT3d.help_backups_why: To go back to a known good setting after tuning, or to copy a setting to another servo.
paramsT3d.help_backups_how: Compare shows what differs from the servo now; Restore and Load put the values in the list of changes, and nothing is written until you press "Write to the servo".

machineProfile.the_profile_doesn_t_say_where: The profile doesn't say where to read the alarm code: the table is for reference only.
machineProfile.device_returned_other: {name}: the device returned {v}, not what was written
machineProfile.help_params_what: The registers of the device that its JSON profile describes: register, name, current value and allowed range. Tap a row for its description, options, scale and factory value.
machineProfile.help_params_why: To read and, when the profile says the register is writable, change the settings of a device that is not the T3D servo.
machineProfile.help_params_how: Read all asks every register; the eye icon marks the ones read every cycle and the pencil the writable ones. Writing needs a second tap to confirm.
machineProfile.help_alarms_what: The alarm codes of the device with their text, cause and what to do, taken from its JSON profile. The one active now is highlighted.
machineProfile.help_alarms_why: To understand a code without opening the manual.
machineProfile.help_alarms_how: The active code comes from the register the profile names for it. Without that register the table is only a reference.

rS485.lead: The devices connected through RS485: devices, buses and adapters, and diagnostics.
rS485.marked_as_absent_it_no_longer: Marked as absent: it no longer counts as a fault.
rS485.there_are_unsaved_changes_in_the: There are unsaved changes in the buses.
rS485.to_remove_it_first_move_or: To remove it, first move or remove its devices.
rS485.own_m575_command_replaces_the_one: Own M575 command (replaces the one above)
rS485.if_nothing_answers_on_one_port: . If nothing answers on one port, try the other.
rS485.and_the_plugin_asks_it_for: ) and the plugin asks it for the readings. Connect the device's A/B to the Duet's RS485 terminals. When used, it sends:
rS485.the_duet_acts_as_the_modbus: The Duet acts as the Modbus master (RRF 3.6:
rS485.no_address_answered_check_speed_format: No address answered (check speed, format and A/B wiring)
rS485.save_the_changes_to_search_with: save the changes to search with the new speed and format
rS485.no_usb_rs485_adapter_connected_plug: No USB-RS485 adapter connected. Plug it into a USB port on the system and tap Refresh.
rS485.could_not_read_the_list_of: Could not read the list of adapters.
rS485.the_service_isn_t_allowed_to: The service isn't allowed to use serial ports. Once, on the system (SSH):
rS485.its_faults_only_warn_until_you: : its faults only warn until you review it and assign one. You get a notice in Activity and on the phone.
rS485.its_faults_only_warn_until_you_no_activi: : its faults only warn until you review it and assign one. You get a notice on the phone.
rS485.add_them_automatically_no_axis_they: Add them automatically (no axis, they only warn)
rS485.first_create_a_bus_in_buses: First create a bus in Buses and adapters.
rS485.no_devices_yet_add_the_first: No devices yet. Add the first one (for example your T3D servo).
rS485.if_they_are_not_connected_on: If they are not connected on purpose: they stop being watched and counted as faults
rS485.the_plugin_service_isn_t_responding: The plugin service isn't responding. Check in Plugins that WorkshopRS485 is started.
rS485.one_new_device: A new unconfigured device showed up on RS485.
rS485.n_new_devices: {n} new unconfigured devices showed up on RS485.
rS485.detection_note: If you connect a new adapter, the system tries every speed and format until something answers and creates its bus. On the buses you already have, every {min} min it looks for new addresses (1-{max}), never during a job. What shows up is added
rS485.bus_note: One bus = one adapter (or the Duet's RS485). A bus can have several devices, each with its address, all at the same speed and format. The system is the only master: do not connect another program to the same adapter.
rS485.register_added: Register {n} added to {name}: give it a name, scale and limits in Edit.
rS485.json_profile_hint: For a device that is not the T3D servo: it is added as «Generic Modbus» and a .json file with its registers and alarms is loaded into it.
rS485.help_detection_what: The system looks for RS485 devices by itself: when you plug a new adapter it tries every speed and format until something answers and creates its bus, and on the buses you already have it looks for new addresses now and then, never during a job.
rS485.help_detection_why: So a new servo shows up without you having to know its address, speed or format.
rS485.help_detection_how: Turn the two switches on or off, or press "Search everything now". Found devices appear below to add or ignore; with the second switch they are added without axis.
rS485.help_buses_what: A bus is one adapter (a USB RS485 adapter or the RS485 of the Duet) and the speed and format used on its cable. A bus can have several devices, each with its own address.
rS485.help_buses_why: The system is the only master of the cable, so it must be set once per adapter and every device on it must match.
rS485.help_buses_how: Do not connect another program to the same adapter. Edit the fields and save; "Find devices" is available after saving.
rS485.help_port_what: The USB serial port of the adapter on the Raspberry Pi (for example /dev/ttyUSB0). You can pick one of the detected adapters or type it.
rS485.help_port_why: It tells the system which adapter belongs to this bus.
rS485.help_port_how: Pick it from the list of adapters connected to the system; the fixed names are better than ttyUSB0 because they do not change when you replug.
rS485.help_baud_what: Baud rate and data format (parity and stop bits) of the cable, for example 19200 8N1.
rS485.help_baud_why: Every device on the bus must use exactly the same values or none will answer.
rS485.help_baud_how: Copy them from the device settings (for the T3D servo, P-182 and P-183). If you do not know them, use automatic detection or the sweep in Diagnosis.
rS485.help_advanced_what: Stop bits, how long to wait for a reply (timeout), the gap between messages and how many times a request is retried.
rS485.help_advanced_why: Slow or noisy devices sometimes need more time or more retries to be read reliably.
rS485.help_advanced_how: Leave the defaults unless a device answers badly: raise the timeout or the gap first, then the retries.

startup.title: Start-up
startup.state_na: does not apply to your machine
startup.make_tip: Copies the example to the SD card. It never overwrites a file that already exists.
startup.edit_tip: Opens the file in the DWC editor.
startup.hide_tip: Hides this row on this screen. It does not delete anything.
startup.service_tip: It has to be running: it makes the examples and answers the buttons of this plugin.
startup.service_sign_in: needs you to sign in to be checked
startup.service_role: your role cannot check it: a technician is needed
startup.locked: Not signed in: sign in to create or change files from here.
startup.row_service_tip: This plugin has its own service (WorkshopRS485), which talks to the adapter. It does not need WorkshopService. It must be running in Settings > Plugins.
startup.assist_tip: Walks you through what is missing, one thing at a time. You can skip what you do not need.
startup.assist_no_action: This cannot be fixed with a file from here. Read the explanation and, when you have it, tap "Check again".
startup.assist_done_ready: Everything you went through is ready.
startup.assist_done_left: {n} left to do. You can start again whenever you like.
startup.create_help_tip: Asks a few questions and builds the file. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
startup.questions_intro: Answer and I will build the file. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
startup.err_range: The number is outside the allowed range.
startup.err_chars: Do not use quotes, semicolons or line breaks.
startup.err_pattern: It does not have the expected format. See the help of this field.
startup.warn_moves: {n} line(s) that move the machine were commented out with ";". Check them and remove the ";" only when you are sure and the machine is free.
startup.warn_active: Lines without ";" really run when you use the button.
startup.plan_example: {file} only has the example (all commented). It is replaced by this one, and the previous text is kept in {backup}.
startup.plan_new: {file} already has your configuration and I will not overwrite it. This one will be saved apart as {target}; when you have checked it, rename it in Files > Macros.
startup.verify_ok: Done: the file exists, has active instructions and the plugin already sees it.
startup.verify_new: Saved as {file}. The plugin keeps using the previous file until you swap the names.
startup.verify_comments: {file} was saved, but all its lines are still commented, so the plugin still takes it as an example. That may be what you wanted.
startup.verify_notseen: {file} was saved, but the plugin does not see it as ready yet. Tap "Check again" in a few seconds.
startup.verify_missing: I could not read {file} back. Tap "Check again" to verify it.
startup.verify_fail: It could not be saved ({error}). Nothing was changed.
startup.plan_changed: The file changed while you were answering. Check again what is going to happen and confirm once more.
startup.modal_hint: Tap a card to set it up, or let it walk you through step by step.
startup.modal_sub: Get ready what this plugin needs from your machine
startup.row_service_what: A service of this plugin (WorkshopRS485) that talks to the RS485 adapter.
startup.row_service_for: Without it the page can neither read nor send anything on the bus.
startup.row_service_missing: There is no communication. Start it in Settings > Plugins.
